input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The shape check before Editor.edit_files tests only for os.PathLike and no longer wraps a plain str, so a string filename is passed on as an iterable and consumed character by character when building the editor command.
- failure path: click.edit(filename="notes.txt") launches the editor with the nine single-character files n, o, t, e, s, ., t, x, t instead of notes.txt; saving creates stray files in the working directory and the intended file is never opened.

Reviewer finding
- description: The single-file check was changed to `isinstance(filename, os.PathLike)`, so a plain `str` filename is no longer wrapped in a tuple.
- rationale: Trigger: calling `click.edit(filename="notes.txt")` with a str. A str is not an os.PathLike, so the wrap at line 907 is skipped and `filename` is passed to `ed.edit_files` as a bare string, which iterates per character. Mechanism: the editor is invoked with each character as a separate filename (e.g. "n", "o", "t"...) instead of the one file. Impact: the user's editor opens wrong or nonexistent paths, and the intended file is never edited, a regression for the common str case.
critique: The finding identifies the same faulty check: `isinstance(filename, os.PathLike)` skips wrapping a plain str. It also gives the same consequence: edit_files iterates the string character by character, so the editor opens single-character files instead of notes.txt.
